newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain 1-yr bill yields seen stable at Tuesday sale.
newsitem.headline: Spain 1-yr bill yields seen stable at Tuesday sale.

text.p: Tuesday's auction of Spanish one-year Treasury bills should see yields unchanged from the previous sale's 6.503 percent, dealers said on Monday.
On the grey market one-year bills are currently trading at a yield of 6.50/6.55 percent.
"The minimum yield will be close to 6.50 percent. If anything we could see a small increase, which will depend on the amount of bids and the Treasury's choice," said one dealer.
At the previous allocation on October 16, one-year bill yields marked a historic low at 6.503 percent, down from 6.751 percent.
The amount bid and allocated should also be around the previous auction's level, dealers said.
The Bank of Spain's key money market rate is 6.75 percent.
